rootCause: 333 apps (5-layer WASM stack) lack process-level isolation. Multiple app instances in single wasm32-unknown-unknown module share linear memory, globals, and WebRTC peer state. OOM, runaway app, or cryptographic key leakage impacts all peers in room.
recommendation: Implement multi-instance WASM sandbox via (1) wasmtime Module + Instance Pool (separate linear mem per app, fuel metering, WASI adapter), (2) 333-CapabilitySet gating (Ed25519 capability tokens per app), (3) ServiceContext as syscall proxy (all app→kernel transitions validated). Start with fuel metering (CPU limit ~100K ops/block), then memory limits (per-app 32MB heap), then capability ACL (block,transfer,burn granularity).
alternatives: Alt1: wasm-bindgen + WASM Component Model (wasi-preview2) — standardized capabilities, but slower; suitable for future multi-language app ecosystem
Alt2: V8 Isolates (Node.js vm module) — full isolation, higher overhead; overkill for single-node consensus
Alt3: Lightweight eBPF in WASM (wasm-micro-runtime) — minimal sandbox, no memory protection; risky for untrusted apps
Alt4: NO sandbox — accept shared-memory risk; workable for closed testnet, unacceptable for production with 3rd-party apps
caveats: Fuel metering requires calibration per validator hardware (CPU speed variance ±20%). WASI adapter introduces ~2-5% overhead. Capability model only works if apps are cryptographically signed (verify at registration via ValidatorKeyring). Cross-instance shared state (e.g., global ledger) must use message-passing, not shared memory.

technicalDetails.wasmtimeArchitecture: Each app = separate wasmtime::Instance bound to InstancePre<T>. Instance holds: (1) own linear memory (32MB default), (2) WASI adapter (file, env, exit), (3) fuel meter (init to 100K ops, decremented per instr), (4) host callbacks (back into 333::kernel via ServiceContext)
technicalDetails.capabilityModel: 333's Ed25519 ValidatorKeyring is capability root. Each app registration creates Capability(app_id, validator_pubkey, operations:[Block, Transfer, Burn]). Before app invokes WASM syscall (place_block, submit_transfer), kernel checks: caller_cert.operations.contains(op). Uses puter Microkernel P3 pattern (sourcePath: src/kernel/capability.rs, confidence=0.92)
technicalDetails.serviceContextPattern: Platform333 WASM struct (src/wasm.rs:15) holds Executor + HLC + LWW-Map + HotStuff state. ServiceContext wraps this as RPC handler: app→invoke(HLC, delta, signature) → kernel validates → app can proceed. All I/O forbidden; only state mutations via LWW-Map deltas.
technicalDetails.memoryEnforcement: wasmtime::Store::limiter() + MemoryCreator. Each Instance gets Store with max_memory=32MB + max_table_elements=1000. OOM trap on overflow.
technicalDetails.fuelMeteringCalibration: Baseline: 100K fuel = 1 block execution (~20ms). Adjust per op: simple arithmetic=1, hash=50, signature verify=5000. Per-block budget = (blocktime_ms / 20) * 100K.

designDecisions.rationale: wasmtime is ~10x faster (JIT), fuel metering is production-tested (polkadot-sdk uses it), API is stable
designDecisions.tradeoff: ~2MB binary size increase, requires no_std runtime for WASM components

designDecisions.rationale: Aligns with 333's cryptographic foundation (PublicKeyStore). Each app signs its capability intent; validator verifies signature before grant
designDecisions.tradeoff: Requires app to embed validator public key; offline capability revocation requires ledger entry

designDecisions.decision: Separate linear memory per Instance (not shared heap arena)
designDecisions.rationale: WASM spec guarantees memory isolation at language level. No need for userspace GC or arena allocator
designDecisions.tradeoff: Per-app overhead ~32MB; 50 apps = 1.6GB resident memory. Mitigate: lazy-load apps, swap out inactive ones

designDecisions.decision: ServiceContext as RPC proxy (not raw WASM imports)
designDecisions.rationale: All app→kernel transitions go through one validated handler. Easier to log, meter, and revoke
designDecisions.tradeoff: Slightly higher latency (~1-2µs per call); acceptable for on-chain operations

integrationPoints: HotStuff block validation → call app_instance.execute_block() with fuel meter active
ValidatorKeyring (crypto module) → add capability_registry: Map<app_id, CapabilitySet>
LWW-Map merge_delta hook → intercept app state changes, apply capability ACL
WASI adapter → restrict file/env access to app-specific sandbox dirs
riskMitigation: Risk: Fuel calibration wrong → app starves. Mitigation: fuzzy-test fuel consumption on all block types, add observability metric app_fuel_remaining
Risk: App finds memory overflow exploit → crash entire platform. Mitigation: run e2e test suite with >100K randomly-generated app bytecodes (fuzzing)
Risk: Capability signature verification fails → unauthorized app gains power. Mitigation: audit ValidatorKeyring::verify() with Taliban lens (constitutional + mathematical)
Risk: WASI adapter leaks filesystem access → app reads other apps' data. Mitigation: isolate sandbox dirs per app_id, use seccomp-style allowlist for syscalls

performance.instance_creation_throughput_per_sec: 20 (reasonable for registration, not on hot path)

oneLineSummary: Multi-instance WASM sandbox (wasmtime) + Ed25519 capability ACL + ServiceContext RPC proxy isolates untrusted 333 apps; fuel metering ensures bounded CPU, per-instance memory limits prevent OOM DoS, capability tokens enforce op granularity (Block/Transfer/Burn).
